x_axis_error_verdict.question: Does x_axis_error exist (i.e. are commanded and actual X position both exposed as separate columns)?
x_axis_error_verdict.answer: YES â€” CONFIRMED. hfdata.csv carries BOTH 'DES_POS|n' (CommandedAxisPosition, per header.csv) and 'ENC_POS|n' (ActualAxisPosition) as separate columns for every axis index present. x_axis_error = DES_POS|<x-index> - ENC_POS|<x-index> is directly derivable exactly as the card's contract specifies. This resolves the card's single largest open risk item in the card's favor.
x_axis_error_verdict.axis_index_to_letter_mapping: INFERRED, NOT explicitly documented in the public package. header.csv's template defines axis indices 1-6 for every signal type, but the ACTUAL hfdata.csv rows only populate indices |1, |2, |3, |6 (indices 4 and 5 are template slots that never appear in real data). Given the machine is a 3-axis (X/Y/Z) horizontal milling center plus one main spindle, the most parsimonious reading is 1=X, 2=Y, 3=Z, 6=Spindle â€” but this is domain-convention inference, not a labeled fact from KIT. TBD: confirm by cross-correlating DES_POS|1/2/3 trajectories against the known X/Y/Z coordinates in the per-experiment NC G-code files (Data/Descriptive/Part description/<component>/nc_data/*.nc, present in the archive) before ml-modeler commits to which index is X.
x_axis_error_verdict.bonus_finding_not_a_substitution: hfdata.csv ALSO carries a native 'CTRL_DIFF|n' (ControlDiff) column per axis, which by name is very likely the Siemens controller's own precomputed following-error signal (commanded minus actual, or a closely related quantity) â€” a second, native path to the same physical quantity the card asks for. This is reported as an additional option, not proposed as a silent substitute for the card's explicit DES_POS-minus-ENC_POS derivation; ml-modeler should pick one and record which.

_anomaly_composition_finding_M2.source: DoE_dump.tsv, all 33 experiments, read in full (no download needed)
_anomaly_composition_finding_M2.headline: The 15 anomalous experiments are THREE different phenomena. Only one is this use case.

machine_tool_condition_GENUINE_DRIFT.note: Cutting parameters IDENTICAL to the IM-01R baseline; the difference is real tool wear (A01/A02 also carry blowholes at 1mm/5mm). Maps to use-case drift_class: tool_wear.

commanded_parameter_change_LEAKAGE_RISK.note: The machine was TOLD to run differently (Feedrate+20%, Overload +30%/+60%, Built-up edge f_z-30%/v_c-30%, Chatter via f_z 0.02246->0.04492, irregular stock allowance).
commanded_parameter_change_LEAKAGE_RISK.leakage: The changed setting is ALSO an input column: hfdata.csv carries CMD_SPEED|n and the feedrate is encoded in the DES_POS trajectory. A model can score near-perfectly by reading commanded feedrate -- learning "this program was configured differently", not "this machine is drifting". On a real line the commanded feedrate is normal, so such a model detects nothing: excellent in eval, worthless on PWT-LINE-3.

workpiece_defect_DIFFERENT_USE_CASE.note: Cavities axial, Cavity radial, Cracks, Chipped Edge. Cutting parameters byte-identical to the IMP-01 baseline (overlap 2.5, depth 8, fz 0.03, 8000 rpm, feed 480) -- the PART was defective, not the machine.
workpiece_defect_DIFFERENT_USE_CASE.belongs_to: a material/quality-escape objective (cf. the separate quality-escape-shipment-containment use case), not machine-performance drift

_anomaly_composition_finding_M2.consequence: Restricted to genuine machine drift, the usable signal is 5 anomalous experiments on ONE component type and ONE material against 2 normal baselines. Thin for a 1D-CNN. Drives the M3 taxonomy decision and very likely makes M4 /synth-data necessary rather than optional.
